newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Angola's UNITA says all former fighters in camps.
newsitem.headline: Angola's UNITA says all former fighters in camps.

text.p: Angola's former rebel movement UNITA said it had finished confining its guerrilla fighters to U.N. camps and had handed over their weapons to U.N. observers under a 1994 peace agreement reached with the government.

UNITA spokesman Isaias Samakuva said in a statement that, in addition, 463 of the movement's "police force" would be confined to camps in the next few days, with the agreement of the joint commission in charge of the peace process.
Samakuva said in the statement presented to U.N. special representative Alioune Blondin Beye on Wednesday that UNITA would continue to keep a guard for its leader, Jonas Savimbi.

The U.N. Angola Verification Mission, numbering 7,000 troops and military observers, is monitoring implementation of a 1994 peace deal signed in Zambia that ended nearly two decades of civil war between the Angolan government and UNITA (the National Union for the Total Independence of Angola).

UNITA's slowness in handing over weapons and confining its members to U.N.-run camps has been criticised by monitors overseeing the process. They accused the former rebels of dragging their feet and the U.N. threatened diplomatic and financial sanctions on UNITA if it did not hurry up disarmament.
The U.N. Security Council on Wednesday approved a final extension of the mandate of the U.N. peacekeeping force until February 28.

The U.N. resolution urged the Angolan government to avoid offensive military operations beyond those strictly necessary for the restoration and maintenance of law and order in areas formerly occupied by UNITA.
Both sides were called on to intensify efforts to clear millions of mines sown during the war and to destroy stockpiles under UNAVEM monitoring.
